THE FAIR QUESTION

“Why not just drop
all the files into Claude?”

For a few files and a one-off question, that can work well. But a growing archive of monitoring reports needs more than a bigger chat window.

A ONE-OFF FILE CHAT

A useful place to start.

Uploading a file doesn’t mean every row stays in the model’s working context. Context windows are finite, and recall can weaken as the amount of text grows. A long conversation alone is not a dependable record of an entire reporting archive.

YOUR RECURRING PR WORKFLOW
The archive lives outside the chat

Monitoring batches and structured reporting data stay in the project database, beyond the model’s working context.

Analysis tools do the data work

The assistant uses project analysis tools and scoped results, rather than relying on the full archive being pasted into a prompt.

Context you can check

Select the files, brands, and periods behind a comparison. Keep sentiment, article type, and relevance labels available for repeated reporting.

Connected outputs

Move from AI questions to charts and Excel or PowerPoint reports.

Store the archive. Analyze the selected data. Give the AI the relevant evidence. That is the advantage—not a promise of unlimited AI memory or error-free answers.

Why context limits matter—and what still needs review

Claude and other AI products can use retrieval, code, and context management to work with larger datasets. The distinction here is the built-in PR data and reporting workflow, not an absolute limit on what another system can do. Read Anthropic’s explanation of context and recall ↗

Separate measured facts from hypotheses. Check the selected brands, files, and dates; review classifications and recommendations against the sources. Estimated reach is not unique audience, and coverage alone does not prove revenue.

Export scope: project and comparison exports are available in Excel and PowerPoint. Editorialized presentations from selected Chat exchanges remain on the roadmap.

MAKE THE BUSINESS CASE

What would you do
with those hours back?

Think about the hours spent combining monitoring reports, reviewing mentions, comparing periods, and preparing client decks. Put your own numbers in and see what less manual work could be worth.

START WITH A SCENARIO

Scenario inputs, not pricing or measured product results. Time saved represents capacity; it becomes cash savings only if actual costs fall. Human review remains part of the work.

YOUR ESTIMATED ANNUAL CAPACITY VALUE

Hours freed / month
Annual value after investment
Modeled net ROI
Break-even time reduction
Show the math

Monthly hours freed = reports × hours per report × time reduction.
Annual capacity value = monthly hours freed × hourly cost × 12.
Net value = capacity value − annual investment.
ROI = net value ÷ annual investment × 100.
